paragraph: Learning rate beyond the grid edge (post hoc). HQ and C-matched both use 3 × 10⁻³, the upper edge of the grid from which they were selected. Under an analysis plan fixed by hash before the runs, HQ was therefore re-trained at 10⁻² on the same 36 blocks. HQ (10⁻²) − C-matched (3 × 10⁻³) AUC was −0.0055 [−0.0105, −0.0005] (two-sided p = 0.033; HQ lower in 69% of blocks; Table 11), and HQ (10⁻²) − HQ (3 × 10⁻³) was +0.0032 [−0.0014, +0.0078]. HQ therefore still learned less than C-matched at the next learning rate, although the gap was smaller than at its selected rate (B-H1, −0.0087) and HQ's own area rose further, without resolution. Moving HQ one half-decade beyond its grid did not remove the deficit; higher rates were not tested. Mean final-checkpoint weighted J was 0.028 for HQ at 10⁻², 0.023 at 3 × 10⁻³ and 0.039 for C-matched. The circuit angles moved little in absolute terms (median mean |Δθ| 0.052 rad at 3 × 10⁻³ and 0.078 rad at 10⁻²), but by a fraction of their small initial values (median mean |θ| 0.076 rad) similar to that of the classical head weights: the median relative change ‖Δθ‖/‖θ₀‖ was 0.77 at 3 × 10⁻³ and 1.18 at 10⁻², against 0.78 and 0.53 for the head's classical projection and readout at 3 × 10⁻³ (descriptive, not in the plan). Small absolute angle changes therefore do not by themselves show that the circuit was untrained.
clause: also at a higher hybrid learning rate
conclusion: HQ's lower area than C-matched persisted when HQ was re-trained at the next learning rate, 10⁻².
